findings.summary: The implementer report claims 'Tests for the change were written and run,' but the diff touches only historical-sync-consumer.server.ts — no test file is part of this commit. The existing test file (__tests__/historical-sync-consumer.server.test.ts) was not modified and contains zero tests exercising the Intervals.icu path at all (fetchIntervalsActivities, hasMoreIntervals, MAX_INTERVALS_PAGES) — every 'source branching' test uses a Strava payload. The actual behavior this task changes (per-source continuation signal, hard page cap) has no automated coverage, and the report's claim about tests is false.

findings.summary: hasMoreIntervals uses `payload.page <= MAX_INTERVALS_PAGES`, checked against the *current* page before incrementing. If every page up to and including page 24 returns activities, page 25 still gets queued and fetched (25 <= 24 is only false once page reaches 25), so the Intervals.icu path actually walks 25 pages, not the 24 the constant/comment ('2 months per page = ~4 years') implies. Still hard-bounded (satisfies the brief's 'can't run away indefinitely' requirement), just one page past the stated cap. Using `payload.page < MAX_INTERVALS_PAGES` would match the comment's intent exactly.
